subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What public web-tool egress boundary should OpenClaw expose for domain allow/deny controls: a scoped web_fetch allowlist/denylist, a cross-tool fetch/search/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: The requested config would be treated as a security boundary by operators, and the current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while leaving deny-domain, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs and define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, caches, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy As Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through proxy.enabled and external operator policy instead of adding a local domain firewall to web tools.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while leaving deny-domain, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest visible history across web_fetch, SSRF, guarded fetch, and docs touched by this boundary choice.
